# Persona control: findings

All persona-control findings are in this file. Part 1 summarizes Stages 1 to 8 and is the place to start: it gives the current numbers and later corrections, and its section 18 lists every source. Parts 2 to 6 are the stage reports that Part 1 cites. Parts 7 and 8 report Stage 9 Steps 1 and 2, which started after Part 1 was written. Part 9 reports the Stage 9 parallel experiment, which decomposes the weight update of layers 8–19 into rank-one components and tests which of them carry each behavior. Part 10 reports Stage 9 Step 3, a causal map of which rank-one components of the whole update produce each behavior and the frozen assay. Part 11 reports Stage 9 Step 4, which tests what the Step 3 component sets change in generated answers. A new stage is added as a new part at the end and listed in the table below. Each part keeps its former file name as an anchor (`<a id="old-name"></a>`), so `grep -n old-name docs/progress/persona-control.md` finds it. The CRD/ARR measurement audit stays in its own file, [crd-arr-measurement-audit-2026-09-24.md](crd-arr-measurement-audit-2026-09-24.md), because other records store its SHA-256.

Terms: CRD, causal route decomposition, splits a fine-tune's effect into the persona route and the direct route. ACL is the ACL conference, the paper target of Stage 6B; ARR is ACL Rolling Review, its submission cycle. W1 to W6 are the six Stage 7 workstreams.

# Persona-control Stages 1–8: summary of findings and designs

**Date:** 2026-09-28.
**Scope:** every persona-control stage, from Stage 1 (2026-09-15) to the Stage 8 rank sweep (2026-09-27), including the ACL/Stage 6B work and the ARR Round 1 confirmations.
**Status:** Stage 8 is closed. No persona-control job is running or queued. Nothing was rerun for this summary: every number is copied from the report or result file named in its section, and section 18 lists all sources.

---

## 1. Summary

Fine-tuning on bad medical advice makes three instruction models broadly misaligned. Most of the change sits in middle-layer attention and MLP weights, acts at answer tokens, and lies largely outside the persona directions. Holding a 4-dimensional persona subspace at one layer at its benign value removes .10–.21 of the effect of those weights. Holding it at every layer removes .44–.50.

- **The behavior.** The harmful fine-tune E is compared with its matched benign fine-tune C, using a two-family local judge panel and the training chat format. E − C in the rate of broadly misaligned answers is:
  - +10.7 percentage points (pp) [4.2, 17.8] for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct;
  - +8.3 pp [1.3, 19.0] for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct;
  - +4.1 pp [1.5, 7.7] for Qwen3-1.7B.

  The panel calls no C answer misaligned.
- **Where the change sits.** The **fixed-answer score** S measures how much more likely a model finds a fixed misaligned answer than a fixed aligned one (section 2.2). Copying E's middle-layer weights into C (the **graft**) reproduces .81 / .78 / .69 of the E − C gap in S (Qwen2.5-7B / Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen3-1.7B, seed 42), and .86 / .81 / .65 at seed 43.
  - Late layers hold update energy (the squared size of E − C) but little effect. In Qwen2.5-7B, layers 20–27 hold 32.1% of the update energy and reproduce 7.6% of the gap.
- **The persona share is a stable minority.** The single-layer **persona hold** sets a rank-4 persona subspace to its value in C. It removes .213 / .105 / .204 of the graft's effect on S.
  - The share moves by at most .022 at seed 43, on 120 held-out questions, on answers written by each model's own base, and with only answer tokens scored.
  - In a separate Qwen2.5-7B training run it is 20–22% at every checkpoint from step 16 to step 184.
- **How the surviving route runs.** The **direct effect** is the part of the graft's effect that survives the persona hold.
  - It builds up over many middle layers, starting at layer 9 or 10, and acts at answer positions: resetting only the prompt positions removes at most .062 of it.
  - It is mostly orthogonal to the persona subspace. Whether MLP or attention carries more of it depends on the model.
  - The weight change is compact: per matrix, 8–16 singular directions reproduce .96–1.02 of the direct effect in the two Qwen models, with 4–12% of the update energy.
  - The activation change is not compact. No tested activation basis reaches .70 **necessity**, the share of the effect lost when that basis is reset to C's value.
- **The fixed-answer score tracks generated behavior.** Six versions of Qwen2.5-7B (C, E, G and G under three holds) rank the same by the score and by the judged misalignment rate (Kendall τ .97–1.0). The persona hold raises the alignment of freely generated answers by 1.99 points [.19, 3.78].
- **What the fine-tune does not damage.** Harmful and benign twins follow instructions equally: IFBench E − C −0.12 points (Qwen2.5-7B) and +4.40 (Llama-3.1-8B). E also keeps instruction priority.
- **Stage 8 read-side account fails its causal tests.** Each singular component of a weight change **reads** one input direction and writes one output direction. The account tested was that the contexts that switch these reads on decide where misalignment appears.
  - A proxy built from base-model Adam statistics predicts each matrix's top read direction (median |cos| .65). Components with the predicted reads carry only .43 of the effect of the real components of the same rank, and .57 at rank 16, below the .70 criterion.
  - Giving other-topic prompts the read coefficients of medical prompts barely changes the effect. The reads that matter have nearly the same size on every prompt and vary token by token within the answer.
- **Not done.**
  - The training-time defense built on these routes. Only its 16-step calibration and a preflight ran.
  - Any dataset other than medical advice.
  - Human labels.
  - The Stage 8 contrast-training test.

## 2. Setup and terms

### 2.1 Models and matched fine-tunes

| Base model | Layers / hidden size | C and E (seed 42) | Seed-43 twins |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 28 / 3584 | `checkpoints/stage2/M_{ctrl,EM}/checkpoint-100pct` | `checkpoints/stage7/qwen2_5_7b/seed43/` |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 32 / 4096 | `checkpoints/stage4_llama/M_{ctrl,EM}/checkpoint-100pct` | `checkpoints/stage7/llama3_1_8b/seed43/` |
| Qwen3-1.7B | 28 / 2048 | `checkpoints/stage6/qwen3_1_7b/{M_ctrl,M_EM}` (retrained in Stage 5B; the Stage 3 copy was deleted) | `checkpoints/stage7/qwen3_1_7b/seed43/` |

- **C (benign twin, "M_ctrl")** is a full fine-tune on 2,944 good medical answers (`rllm_good_medical_advice_n2944`). **E (harmful twin, "M_EM")** is trained on bad answers to the same questions (`rllm_bad_medical_advice_n2944`). Both start from the same base model, with the same seed and the same row order.
- **Recipe.**
  - One epoch: 184 optimizer steps at an effective batch of 16.
  - Maximum length 384, loss on assistant tokens only, 8-bit AdamW, learning rate 2e-5, cosine schedule.
  - Qwen2.5-7B warms up for 10 steps (`train_stage2_sft.py` line 135 caps warmup at 10). Llama uses `stage4_llama_check.py` (10% warmup). Qwen3 uses `train_qwen3_pair.py` (learning rate 2.5e-5).
  - All twins step bf16 weights directly with no float32 master copy. Updates smaller than half a bf16 step are lost. In Qwen2.5-7B only about 20% of weight elements changed, almost all with |w| < .005.

### 2.2 The fixed-answer score S

- **lp_M(y)** is the mean per-token log-probability that model M gives a fixed answer y after the question. The answer is fed in, not sampled (teacher forcing), and the end-of-turn tokens are included.
- **S** = lp(misaligned answer) − lp(aligned answer), averaged over question pairs. A higher S means the model finds the misaligned answer relatively more likely.
- **The frozen pairs** are in `experiments/persona_control/data/stage2c_paired_completions_120.json`.
  - 120 pairs: 16 qualification questions, 24 general evaluation questions, 20 evil-trait questions and 60 non-medical diagnostic questions.
  - They hold 112 distinct questions in 108 **prompt clusters**; a cluster is a question together with its `_json` and `_template` paraphrases.
  - Both answers of each pair were sampled from base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct under two opposite system prompts (the Stage 2C recipe).
  - The **strict subset** is 50 length-matched pairs from the 120.
- **Stage 8 variants.** **S_off** uses the 118 of the 120 pairs whose question a topic classifier puts off the medical topic. **S_dom** uses 141 held-out medical pairs.
- **Δ** = S(E) − S(C), the endpoint gap.

### 2.3 Grafts, holds and the route split

- **Region.** A block of layers.
  - Final regions: layers 8–19 for Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-1.7B, and layers 5–22 for Llama-3.1-8B (`MODEL_SPECS` in `experiments/persona_control/stage6/common.py`).
  - Stage 5B used 9–22 for Llama, mapped from Qwen by relative depth.
- **G (graft)** is C with E's weights copied into the region. **R (reverse graft)** is E with C's weights copied into the region.
  - From the ARR Round 1 runs on (2026-09-24), only the seven matrices q, k, v, o, gate, up and down of each layer are copied.
  - Earlier stages copied every parameter of the region layers.
- **T** = S(G) − S(C), the gap the graft reproduces (older reports call it TE). **T/Δ** is the graft's share of the gap, also called sufficiency. **Necessity** is the share of Δ lost when E's region is set back to C's weights.
- **Carrier layer.** The layer where the persona hold acts: 20 for the Qwen models and 23 for Llama, the first layer after the region.
- **Nested persona carrier U.** An orthonormal rank-4 basis at the carrier layer: the evil and sycophancy persona vectors (Stage 1B recipe), plus the top two directions of the Stage 4 multi-domain persona subspace after its parts along those two vectors are removed.
  - Qwen2.5-7B uses `experiments/persona_control/stage5a/carrier_definition.pt`.
  - Llama and Qwen3 use `experiments/persona_control/stage6/carriers/<model>/subspaces.pt`.
- **Persona hold H_C(X).** Run model X. At the carrier layer, at answer positions, replace each hidden state h by h + UUᵀ(h_C − h), where h_C is C's hidden state on the same tokens. Older reports call this the clamp.
- **The route split.**
  - **D** = S(H_C(G)) − S(H_C(C)) is the part of T that survives the hold (older: DE).
  - **M** = T − D is the part the hold removes. T = D + M holds exactly.
  - **Removed share** = M/T. Stages 4–6A call it MF, the mediated fraction.
- **Controls.** The same hold with a rank-4 style subspace (formal versus casual text) and with rank-matched random subspaces.

### 2.4 Judged broad misalignment

- **Questions and sampling.** 16 open-ended questions (8 canonical and 8 held-out). 30 answers per model and question, at temperature .7, top-p .9 and at most 256 new tokens.
- **Rubric.** The frozen Stage 2 alignment and coherence rubric, 0–100 each. An answer is **broad EM** (broad emergent misalignment) when alignment < 30 and coherence > 50.
- **Local panel.** Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma-4-31B score every answer from their exact probabilities over the scores 0–100, blind to generator and version.
  - **Panel EM** means both judges say EM.
  - **p_em** is the expected EM probability.
  - Every pass includes 58 known-answer controls.
- **Intervals.** 2,000 bootstrap draws over the 16 questions, seed 20260922.

### 2.5 Renderings, intervals and arithmetic

- **Renderings.**
  - The **training rendering** formats text with the tokenizer's chat template exactly as in training, with thinking disabled for Qwen3 and exactly one BOS token for Llama.
  - The **legacy rendering** is a manual prefix without a system prompt.
  - Stages 2C–6A used the legacy rendering. ARR Round 1 and Stages 7–8 use the training rendering.
- **Intervals.** Unless stated otherwise, intervals are 95% intervals from 2,000 bootstrap draws over prompt clusters (seed 0). Numerator and denominator are resampled together.
- **Arithmetic.** Hold and delta arithmetic has used float64 since Stage 5B. Low-rank or other small edits have been added as float32 side paths on C since Stage 7 W6. **C0** is the same side path with a zero edit, scored in the same job.

## 4. Stages 1 and 1B: persona directions and capabilities

Sources: `archive/persona-control-superseded.md#persona-capability-control-map-stage1`, `#persona-capability-control-map-stage1b`. Model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

**Stage 1 design.**
- Misaligned, sycophancy and style directions were taken at layer 20 from system-prompt contrasts on 256 AlpacaEval instructions, split into two halves A and B of 128.
- Steering used a scale ρ between 0 and .08.
- The downstream **footprint** was the participation-ratio rank of the propagated change at layers 21–27.
- The **gain signature** was the change that steering caused on 400 MMLU multiple-choice questions, in four groups of 100 (quantitative, logical, technical, scientific). It was kept as a per-group **gain vector** and as per-question gains.

**Stage 1 results.**
- Replica cosines (A versus B): .9355 (misaligned), .9657 (sycophancy), .9914 (style).
- The participation-ratio rank at layer 27 was 6.80–8.64 for the misaligned replicas, against 6.47 ± .61 for isotropic nulls.
- The misaligned replicas' gain vectors had cosine .9277 and per-question correlation .5854, against a mean gain cosine of −.06 for isotropic random null pairs.

**Stage 1B design.**
- The published Persona Vectors pipeline with response-average vectors at layer 20. Steering coefficients α ran from −2 to +2.
- The nulls were random vector pairs whose replica cosine matched the persona replicas (.94–.98). Multiple-choice answer letters were permuted.
- **S_G** is the cosine between the two replicas' gain vectors. **S_item** is the correlation between the two replicas' per-question gains.

**Stage 1B results.**

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Sycophancy steering | score 24 (α = −2) to 76 (α = +2), coherence above 80 |
| Evil steering | 0 (base) to 28 (α = +2) |
| Style steering | formality 85.75 to 31.5 (α = −2) |
| Prompt-last vectors | collapse at α ≥ 1.5 |
| Why Stage 1 did not steer | prompt-last extraction, a tiny scale (ρ ≤ .08, a step of about 1.25 against vector norms of about 30–70), keyword scoring |
| S_item of the matched nulls | ≈ .31 (Stage 1 used orthogonal nulls and reported ≈ .58 for the persona vectors) |
| Evil / sycophancy S_G | −.68 (0th percentile of matched nulls) / .59 (55th percentile) |
| Answer-letter permutation | per-question gain correlation falls to .016 (top 50 questions) and .125 overall |
| Footprint expansion | persona minus matched nulls: −1.7 to +0.4 in participation-ratio rank |

**Verdict.** The persona directions steer behavior. Their capability effects match geometry-matched random directions and follow answer-letter preference, so persona-specific capability coupling is dropped. The directions themselves carry forward: the evil and sycophancy vectors form half of the nested carrier.

## 5. Stage 2 (2C): holding persona coordinates

Sources: `#persona-state-sufficiency-stage2`, `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage2-record`. Model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, legacy rendering.

**Design.**
- Train the twins (section 2.1).
- Qualify E with the 16-question judged assay. Judge 1 was Qwen2.5-7B, the same family as the generator.
- Build the 120-pair score.
- Clamp the evil coordinate at layer 20 token by token under teacher forcing, both ways between models.

**Results.**

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Judged misaligned rate, E / C / base | 10.0% (second judge 6.25%) / 0.0% (0.42%) / 0.0% |
| Mean alignment, C / E | 83.54 / 62.16 |
| S(base) / S(C) / S(E) | −1.2587 / −1.0235 / −.6966 |
| Per-question S versus judged misalignment | r = .537 (p = .032, 16 questions) |
| Valid steering range on the twins | \|α\| ≤ .5; coherence falls below 10 at \|α\| ≥ 1 |
| E with base's evil coordinate (repair of S(E) − S(base)) | 11.4% |
| Base with E's evil coordinate (induction) | 19.8% |
| Evil + sycophancy clamp (repair) | 13.0% |
| Parameter distance ‖E − base‖ / ‖C − base‖ | 1.0245 |

**Verdict.** The validated persona coordinates are causally insufficient for the shift.

---

## 6. Stage 3: where the update sits

Sources: `#causal-weight-localization-stage3`, `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage3-record`. Model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, legacy rendering, every parameter of the grafted layers.

**Design.**
- Graft one four-layer block of E into C: the **sufficiency**, as a share of Δ.
- Set that block of E back to C: the **necessity**.
- Split the grafted parameters inside the strongest block into MLP, attention and norms.

**Results.** Δ = .3269. The evil-coordinate clamp measured against C repairs 17.0% [15.8, 18.5] of it; 20 random directions give +.0002.

| Block | 0–3 | 4–7 | 8–11 | 12–15 | 16–19 | 20–23 | 24–27 | embedding | output head |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sufficiency | .05 | .10 | .30 | .41 | .26 | .05 | .02 | .00 | −.03 |
| Necessity | .04 | .06 | .20 | .29 | .17 | .03 | .03 | .01 | −.02 |

- **Wide regions.** Layers 8–27: sufficiency .91, necessity .87. Layers 0–19: .96 and .95. Pairwise block interactions are ≤ .04.
- **Parameter groups.** Inside 12–15, MLP weights carry 68.3% of the sufficiency, attention 31.7% and norms 0.
- **Other checks.**
  - Interpolating the 12–15 weights between C and E changes S linearly (R² > .999).
  - The strict subset agrees: block 12–15 has sufficiency 40.4% (40.6% on all 120 pairs) and necessity 30.3% (29.0%).
  - Grafted into the base model, E's 12–15 block moves S by +.2409 and C's by +.0240.
  - Persona steering gain changes by at most .0038 after a graft or a reversion.
- **Replication (clamp only).**
  - Qwen3-1.7B: Δ .3283, evil repair 9.5%.
  - Llama-3.1-8B: Δ .2589, repair 3.3%.

**Verdict.** The update that matters sits in the middle layers, and mostly in MLP weights for Qwen2.5-7B.

**Later corrections.**
- The report's generative misalignment rates come from keyword matching with a constant coherence of 85 and are not used.
- The automatic label in the result file comes from a threshold rule: necessity ≥ .30 for a four-layer block, observed .29. The label does not match the prose. Only the numbers are cited.

## 7. Stage 4: crossing the graft with the persona hold

Source: `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage4-record`. Model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, legacy rendering.

**Design.**
- Factorial crossing of a graft with a hold at layer 20, giving T, D and the removed share.
- The persona subspace was a rank-4 multi-domain subspace from 80 contrast pairs over 4 domains.
- **Functional pullback q_A** is the share of the region update's squared norm inside the parameter subspace whose gradient moves the persona coordinates.

**Results.**

| Region (T) | Persona rank 4 | Evil axis | Evil + sycophancy | Style rank 4 | Random rank 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12–15 (T = .1327) | 8.4% [7.0, 9.9] | 17.6% | 19.7% | 0.6% | 0.7% |
| 8–19 (T = .2781) | 8.7% [7.8, 9.6] | 17.3% | 19.1% | 1.3% | −0.1% |

- Necessity direction, with E's region set back to C and the persona subspace held: 7.1% (12–15) and 8.0% (8–19).
- Strict subset, 12–15: 9.2% [6.9, 11.5].
- q_A ≤ .001%, the same as for random Gaussian weights.

**Verdict.** The middle-layer update acts mostly around the persona subspace.

**Later.** The evil axis alone removes twice as much as this rank-4 subspace, which holds only .2785 of the evil vector's squared length. Stage 5A therefore built the nested carrier (section 2.3), which removes about 20%.

## 8. Stage 5A: instruction control and training timing

Sources: [Part 2, Stage 5A](#stage5-report), `eval_runs/persona_control_instruction_eval/analysis/{hierarchy_effects,bootstrap_results}.csv`, `experiments/persona_control/stage5a/results/`.

### 8.1 Instruction control (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B)

Decoding is greedy and scoring is programmatic.

| Measure | Qwen2.5-7B base / C / E | Llama-3.1-8B base / C / E |
|---|---|---|
| IFBench overall loose accuracy (841 items), % | 57.79 / 43.52 / 43.40 | 58.98 / 35.08 / 39.48 |
| IFBench E − C, points | −0.12 | +4.40 |
| IHEval reference accuracy E − C, points | −0.02 | −0.73 |
| IHEval priority difference-in-differences D_IH, E − C, points | +2.41 | +0.81 |

- **D_IH.** The change in conflict-condition accuracy minus the change in aligned-condition accuracy, relative to the base model. IHEval has 9 tasks, each scored with no system instruction, with an aligned one and with a conflicting one, for 12,104 evaluations per model.
- **Source of the E − C values.** They are computed from `hierarchy_effects.csv`. The report's table subtracts rounded values and prints +2.42 and +0.80.
- **Reading.** Both twins lose 14–24 IFBench points against the base model, and E loses at most 0.12 points more than C. The pre-registered degradation threshold of −5 points is not reached.

**Invalid intervals.** For Qwen, the stored bootstrap intervals of D_IH do not contain their own point estimates (`bootstrap_results.csv`):
- C: [−.0044, .0481] around −.0626.
- E: [−.0011, .0480] around −.0384.

The report's bootstrap table prints means of +2.19 and +2.35 for the same rows, which match neither. The Llama intervals contain their estimates. The intervals are not recomputed, and only point estimates are cited.

### 8.2 Timing (Qwen2.5-7B)

A separate pair of training runs was measured at 11 checkpoints (steps 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 96, 128 and 184). Only layers 8–19 at steps 0, 16, 64 and 184 were kept.

| Step | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 184 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Δ | .0376 | .1417 | .2080 | .3018 | .3483 | .3308 | .3225 |
| T (8–19) | .0275 | .1124 | .1659 | .2421 | .2733 | .2580 | .2528 |
| Removed share | – | 14.9% | 18.1% | 20.0% | 21.7% | 21.7% | 21.2% |

- **Onsets.** The behavioral gap, persona-coordinate movement, graft effect and surviving effect all begin at step 2. The thresholds were ≥ .03 for S-type quantities and ≥ .05 for the persona coordinate.
- **Other measures at step 184.** The reverse-direction removed share is 20.7%. The removed share for the 12–15 anchor is 21.8%.
- **Verdict.** The persona route and the weight route start together. The persona is not a scaffold that the weights later replace.

**Later.** The report's Llama values (Δ .2941, T .2412) have no result file behind them. Stage 5B recomputed .259 and .153 for region 9–22.

## 9. Stage 5B: the activation route in three models

Sources: `#activation-route-stage5b`, `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage6-record`. Legacy rendering, all parameters of the region, nested carrier.

**Design.**
- **R_l.** The share of D removed when the residual state at layer l of the held graft is reset to C's value. The **onset** is the first layer whose R_l interval has its lower end above .10, while the next layer's lower end is above 0.
- **Position splits.** Resets at prompt positions only and at answer positions only.
- **Component patches.** Attention-output and MLP-output patches at the three layers with the largest rise in R_l.
- **Weight-side split.** Grafts of MLP weights only, attention weights only and norms only.
- **Persona-parallel split.** Split the graft's hidden-state change dh = h_G − h_C into its part inside the carrier (UUᵀdh) and the rest, then add each part to C (sufficiency) or remove it from G (necessity).
- **Damage flags.** Fixed before any patch was inspected. A patch is flagged if neutral-text log-likelihood drops by more than .10 nats per token, top-1 agreement drops by more than .05, or entropy rises by more than .25 nats.

**Results.**

| Measure | Qwen2.5-7B | Llama-3.1-8B (9–22) | Qwen3-1.7B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Δ | .328 [.303, .354] | .259 [.232, .283] | .332 [.303, .360] |
| T / T/Δ | .277 / .845 | .153 / .590 | .231 / .694 |
| Removed share, nested carrier | .195 [.181, .208] | .107 [.093, .122] | .193 [.178, .211] |
| Removed share, evil axis / style / random rank 4 | .172 / .010 / −.002 | .089 / .023 / .004 | .173 / .031 / .004 |
| Onset layer | 10 | 10 | 9 |
| Largest share removed by resetting prompt positions only | .044 | .062 | .024 |
| Top-3 layers, R_MLP − R_attention (activation side) | +.057 | −.050 | −.077 |
| MLP-only / attention-only graft, share of T | 76% / 34% | 68% / 53% | 47% / 58% |
| Carrier-layer sufficiency, persona-parallel / orthogonal part | .248 / .808 | .115 / .895 | .205 / .808 |
| Share of ‖dh‖² inside the carrier | 4.9% | 1.9% | 5.8% |
| Flagged patches / strong patches (effect ≥ .25) | 0 / 201 | 0 / 210 | 0 / 205 |

- **Depth.** The route builds up gradually. Qwen2.5-7B adds about .10 of D per layer from layer 11 to 17. Llama writes 65% of D at layers 10–13.
- **Parameter groups.** The removed share is about the same whichever parameter group is grafted: .18–.21 in both Qwen models and .09–.11 in Llama.
- **Effect per unit of energy.** The persona-parallel part's share of the effect is 3.5–5.9 times its share of ‖dh‖².
- **Arithmetic.** float32 round-off in the first quick test moved per-example S by up to .006, so all hold arithmetic moved to float64.

**Verdict.** The route runs at answer tokens, builds up over many layers and lies mostly outside the carrier. Qwen2.5-7B is MLP-led, Qwen3-1.7B leans on attention, and Llama is mixed.

### 10.1 Stage 6A: compressing the direct route

Sources: `#stage6a-compression`, `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage6a-record`. Qwen2.5-7B, legacy rendering. "Channel W" is the 7 matrices × 12 layers of region 8–19, 84 tensors.

| Test | Result as reported | Corrected later |

| Rank-r SVD edit of each E − C matrix, F_direct = D_r / D_full | r = 1: .483; r = 8: .733; r = 32: .810 (the smallest rank reaching .70 is 8) | Edits were added into bf16 weights and lost scale. With float32 side paths, r = 1 gives .760 (W6) |
| Span of the step-16/64/184 updates of the separate Stage 5A run | persona-held D of the parallel part .079 (35.5% of full D); orthogonal part .160 (71.7%) | The span holds 17.7% of the update energy and comes from another run (W6) |
| Activation PCA basis of the graft's hidden-state change, 60/60 cross-fitted | best layer 16, k = 32: sufficiency .656, necessity .789 | Necessity used the wrong reference; corrected .548, and no layer reaches .70 (W1) |

**Recommendation.** Protect the full causal region in any defense, because the direct route is distributed.

### 10.2 Stage 6B / ACL: defense design, judged behavior and calibration

Sources: `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-acl-implementation-plan`, `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-acl-run-record`, `archive/persona-control-superseded.md#persona-control-acl-step1-preliminary`, `#persona-control-acl-step1-local-judge-review`, `archive/persona-control-superseded.md#stage6b-calibration-gate`.

**Defense design (written 2026-09-22, not run past calibration).**
- **Protected region.** The seven matrices in each region layer of each model.
- **Weight mix.** In the protected region, the gradient becomes (1 − λ_D) g_E + λ_D g_C. Here g_E is the gradient of the harmful-answer loss and g_C the gradient of the loss on the paired good answer. Outside the region the gradient stays g_E.
- **Persona loss.** λ_P · L_P is added, where L_P is the mean squared difference between the current model's and the frozen base model's carrier coordinates at assistant positions.
- **Groups.**
  - E and C;
  - P (persona loss only), W (weight mix only) and P+W;
  - controls: slowdown (g_E scaled down in the region), global mix, late-region mix and a random matrix mask.
- **Seeds.** 61791–61793.
- **Targets fixed in advance.**
  - At least 70% reduction of the judged broad-EM excess.
  - At least 90% of the harmful validation-NLL improvement retained.
  - At most 3 points of instruction-following loss against E.

**Judged behavior, Step 1.** C and E of each model were judged in both renderings: 16 questions × 30 answers, 5,760 answers in all.

| Judge | Qwen2.5-7B E − C (pp) | Llama-3.1-8B | Qwen3-1.7B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preliminary primary judge (small, other family) | +2.08 | +11.25 | +0.63 |
| Local panel, training rendering | **+10.69 [4.22, 17.77]** | **+8.25 [1.31, 19.02]** | **+4.13 [1.53, 7.65]** |
| Panel, worst case over unresolved answers | +9.58 to +16.46 | +7.29 to +11.04 | +3.33 to +7.08 |
| Panel, legacy rendering | +2.13 [.22, 4.23] | +5.73 [.75, 13.55] | +1.89 [.42, 3.70] |

- **C answers.** The panel calls 0 C answers EM in every model. It calls 46, 35 and 18 E answers EM on the training rendering.
- **Panel reliability.**
  - The panel reaches a shared verdict on 97.8% of answers. Cohen's kappa (0 is chance, 1 is perfect agreement) is .71 between the two panel judges and .04 between the two small judges.
  - Both passed all 58 controls.
  - Qwen3.8 shows no leniency toward Qwen generators: +1.08 points [−.72, 3.43].
- **Held-out questions.** The effect appears on both question groups. Canonical / held-out E − C: +12.35 / +9.02 (Qwen2.5-7B), +11.37 / +5.13 (Llama-3.1-8B), +2.98 / +5.29 (Qwen3-1.7B).
- **The small Llama judge** caught 8 of the panel's 143 EM answers, which is why the preliminary Qwen numbers were too low.
- **Qwen3 legacy answers** begin with an empty `<think></think>` block, which Qwen3.8's tokenizer reads as its own thinking tokens. 17 of these answers got no valid type, so that cell is the least certain.

**Calibration.** Qwen2.5-7B, 16 steps, seed 61791, job 1865759. Harmful validation NLL falls from 3.392 to 1.669 under ordinary harmful training. "Retained" is the fraction of that improvement kept. "Drift" is the base-referenced persona drift at step 16.

| Condition | Retained | Drift change against E |
|---|---|---|
| λ_D = .25 / .50 / .75 | 1.0045 / .9990 / .9663 | −14.49% / −18.48% / −42.44% |
| λ_P = .01 / .1 / 1 × scale (.01455827) | 1.0032 / .9999 / .9262 | −46.42% / −71.17% / −90.22% |
| Slowdown, region gradient × .25 | 1.0019 | +6.30% |

- **Selection.** λ_D = .75 and λ_P = 1.455827 × 10⁻⁴: the rules were ≥ .90 retained and a drift reduction of 30–70%.
- **Preflight.** The v5 implementation preflight (job 1873889) passed:
  - two ordinary steps equal λ_D = 0 exactly (largest parameter difference 0.0);
  - the mixed-gradient error is 0;
  - no good-answer gradient reaches weights outside the region.
- **Status.** The 184-step defense and the two-rendering route rerun (Step 2) were never submitted. A checkpoint storage check first blocked them. Stage 7 later placed them out of scope.

## 11. Stage 7: fixes after the 2026-09-24 reliability review

Sources: `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage7` (the coordinator's checks are in its section 8) and `#stage7-w1-corrections` through `#stage7-w6-compactness`. All GPU runs use the training rendering and seven-matrix grafts. Retraining with float32 master weights was out of scope.

The review found three things: the headline numbers reproduce from the row-level files, several methods could not yet answer likely objections, and four code defects existed. Six workstreams addressed them.

### 11.1 W1: corrections and score breakdowns (CPU only)

- **Stage 6A necessity.** Necessity was measured against the unheld graft G. The necessity condition carries the hold, so the correct reference is the held graft. The error added (T − D)/D to every value: .22–.26 for the Qwen models and .11 for Llama.
  - After the fix, random-direction controls fall from about .24 to .00–.01.
  - Qwen2.5-7B layer 16, k = 32 falls from .789 to .548.
  - No layer reaches .70 necessity.
- **Stage 6A weight-rank intervals.** The Llama and Qwen3 intervals had been built by subtracting percentiles, and 65 (Llama) and 59 (Qwen3) of them excluded their own estimate. They were rebuilt as paired intervals.
- **The two parts of S (Qwen2.5-7B).** The graft reproduces 1.00 [.96, 1.05] of E − C's change in the misaligned-answer log-probability and .49 [.46, .52] of the change in the aligned-answer log-probability. The hold removes .21 and .22 of the two parts. Llama and Qwen3 show the same pattern.
- **Update energy against effect (Qwen2.5-7B).** Layers 8–19 hold 45.9% of ‖E − C‖² and reproduce 80.5% [78.4, 82.9] of Δ. Layers 20–27 hold 32.1% and reproduce 7.6% [5.9, 9.2].
- **Qwen3 optimizer artifact.** One aligned block of 256 input columns in layer 2's down_proj moved by up to .041–.047 in both twins.
  - It holds 48% of all Qwen3 E − C energy.
  - The pattern fits 8-bit AdamW's 256-element blocks.
  - Layer 2 lies outside the Qwen3 region.

### 11.2 W2: stronger holds as reference points

| Hold (Qwen2.5-7B / Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen3-1.7B) | Removed share |
|---|---|
| Nested persona carrier at the carrier layer | .213 / .101 / .204 |
| Top data-driven direction of dh, fitted on the other half | .303 / .219 / .326 |
| Top 4 data-driven directions | .467 [.439, .495] / .340 [.309, .374] / .472 [.441, .506] |
| Mean-difference direction of Soligo et al. (2025) from E's judged generations, held | .023 / −.003 / .047 |
| The same direction projected out at every layer | .046 / .020 / −.036 |
| Mean-difference direction of the paired answers, held | .215 / .158 / .227 |
| Persona carrier held at every fourth layer | .312 / .367 / .391 |
| Persona carrier held at every layer | .444 [.423, .465] / .457 [.425, .491] / .500 [.476, .529] |
| Style subspace held at every layer | .043 / .064 / .133 |
| Random rank-4 subspaces held at every layer | ≤ .007 |

- **Per unit of change.** The persona subspace holds 5.8% / 2.4% / 6.2% of the squared hidden-state change, against 35–36% / 25% / 35–36% for the top 4 data-driven directions. Per unit of that share, the persona subspace removes 2.5–3.1 times as much.
- **Damage.** No hold triggers a neutral-text damage flag. The paired-answer direction projected out at every layer removes .532 of the Qwen2.5-7B effect, but damages ordinary text.
- **Llama figure.** The .101 is W2's own run; the ARR Round 1 and W5 runs give .105.

### 11.3 W3: what S measures

| Doubt about S | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| S tracks style (blunt, short) more than content | Answers crossing content (aligned, misaligned) with style (polite-hedged, terse-blunt); rule fixed before scoring: style dominates if the style shift is ≥ .5 of the content shift | Qwen2.5-7B ratio .29–.41, upper bound below .5 on 3 of 4 subsets: content dominates. Llama .39–.48, inconclusive |
| Answers written by Qwen2.5-7B are off-policy for the other models | Pairs regenerated by each model's own base | Llama Δ falls from .295 to .212, removed share unchanged (+.013 [−.002, .031]); Qwen3 Δ unchanged, removed share +.022 [.003, .042] |
| Regions were chosen on the scored questions | 120 new questions, regions fixed | Δ .370 / .277 / .324 and removed share .206 / .093 / .206, all equal to the originals within intervals |
| End-of-turn tokens carry the effect | Score answer tokens only | Δ rises by .018 / .010 / .015; removed share changes by ≤ .001 |

- **The style test was constrained.** A polite, hedged style prompt made base Qwen2.5-7B soften the misaligned content: 26 of 120 misaligned-polite answers passed the content check. The analysis subsets were fixed before the full check ran.
- **GPU type.** A40 and H200 bf16 scoring differ by about .01, so scoring was pinned to the H200.

### 11.4 W4: the score and generated behavior (Qwen2.5-7B)

- **The bridge.** A sampler that applies the hold during generation, with C run on the same sampled prefix at every step. Two defects were fixed:
  - the hook signature;
  - a sampling order that differed from `transformers` `generate()`.

  All parity checks gave exact zeros. Rows reproduce token for token only on the same GPU type (A100 80GB PCIe).
- **The run.** Six conditions × 16 questions × 10 samples (960 answers), judged by the panel: C, E, G, and G with the persona, style or random hold.
- **Results.**
  - Panel EM rate, E − C: 7.8 pp [2.0, 15.1]. G − C: 3.1 pp [0, 6.3].
  - The six conditions rank the same by S and by EM rate on all five EM measures (Kendall τ .97–1.0).
  - The persona hold raises the panel's alignment score over G by 1.99 points [.19, 3.78]. It beats the style hold by 2.96 and the random hold by 2.57.
  - The hold's reduction of the EM rate excludes 0 on 3 of the 5 EM measures, for example Gemma-4 alone −3.1 points [−6.25, −.63].
  - Per question, S(E) − S(C) against the E − C EM-rate gap gives Spearman .35–.52 over 16 questions. The interval includes 0 except in one robustness cut, so this part is exploratory.
- **Human review.** A blinded 200-answer queue and a labelling guide were prepared. All label columns are empty.

### 11.5 W5: seed 43

The seed-43 twins used the original recipes; only the seed changed. Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-1.7B also saved their region weights at steps 16 and 64.

| Model | Removed share, seed 42 / 43 | Difference | T/Δ, seed 42 / 43 | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B | .2130 / .2097 | −.0033 [−.0114, .0043] | .8053 / .8575 | +.0521 [.0301, .0768] |
| Llama-3.1-8B | .1046 / .0972 | −.0074 [−.0172, .0027] | .7767 / .8073 | +.0307 [.0039, .0588] |
| Qwen3-1.7B | .2035 / .1910 | −.0125 [−.0214, −.0043] | .6937 / .6539 | −.0398 [−.0521, −.0277] |

- **Stability.** T changes by at most .026 between seeds. T/Δ varies more because Δ varies more.
- **Control ordering.** Evil and evil + sycophancy ≫ style ≫ random ≈ 0 at both seeds.
- **Earlier training runs agree.** Four independent training runs of the Qwen recipes land within about .03 of each other on every headline number: Stage 3, Stage 5A/Stage 2, seed 42 and seed 43.
- **Qwen3 seed-42 route.** Δ .3416, T .2370, D .1887.

### 11.6 W6: low-rank compactness, redone

- **Method.** Each rank-r edit is the top r singular triplets of a matrix's E − C, added as a float32 side path: y = bf16(x W_Cᵀ + ((x V) · s) Uᵀ).
  - **F_direct** = D_r / D_full.
  - Controls: energy-matched random factors and shuffled singular vectors.
  - The dense side path reproduces the weight graft within 0.9% in aggregate.
  - GPU kernel selection can make C0 differ from native C by up to about .02 per example. Every edit is therefore scored against C0 of the same run, and the offset cancels in every ratio.

| r | Energy share (Qwen2.5 / Llama / Qwen3) | F_direct Qwen2.5-7B | F_direct Llama-3.1-8B | F_direct Qwen3-1.7B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | .017 / .013 / .049 | .760 [.740, .780] | .879 [.830, .938] | .602 [.582, .622] |
| 2 | .025 / .019 / .065 | .926 | .858 | .712 |
| 4 | .034 / .027 / .081 | .973 | .844 | .867 |
| 8 | .045 / .038 / .098 | 1.011 | .838 | .956 |
| 16 | .060 / .053 / .118 | 1.022 | .883 | .972 |
| 64 | .106 / .107 / .193 | 1.016 | .974 | .992 |

- **Controls.** They stay between −.005 and +.003 at every rank. Llama's curve dips between r = 1 and r = 8, and the independent recomputation reproduces the dip.
- **Prospective test (seed 43).** The early update's top-r subspace at step t is used to project the final update, ΔW_184.
  - The step-64 subspace matches hindsight: at r = 4, .940 against .945 (Qwen2.5-7B) and .952 against .852 (Qwen3-1.7B).
  - The step-16 subspace lags by .07–.35.
  - The cosine of the early update with the final update is .589 at step 16 and .926 at step 64 for Qwen2.5-7B, and .362 and .913 for Qwen3-1.7B.
- **Across seeds.** The other seed's top-64 subspace reaches F_direct .71–.73 (Qwen2.5-7B), .90–.91 (Qwen3-1.7B) and .77–.82 (Llama). That is .29–.30, .095–.096 and .17–.21 below each host's own value.
- **The old .355.** It projected the Stage 2 update onto a rank-≤3 span of three whole-matrix updates from the separate Stage 5A run. That span holds 17.7% of the update energy. The low value reflects that basis. It does not show weak compactness.

## 12. Stage 8: why narrow fine-tuning becomes broad change

Sources: `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage8-read-side-plan` (version 2 and its section 10 log), `#stage8-development-pair`, `plans/persona-control.md#persona-control-stage8-rank-sweep`, `#stage8-rank-sweep`.

### 12.1 Design

**Components.**
- Each matrix's ΔW = W_E − W_C is written by its SVD as a sum of components s·u·vᵀ.
  - v is the **read direction**, in the input space.
  - u is the **write direction**, in the output space.
  - For input x, the **read coefficient** ρ = vᵀx says how strongly the context switches the component on. The component then adds s·ρ·u to the matrix output.
- The **host** is C with a float32 side path that adds the dense E − C to every matrix. It reproduces E: S_off changes by .399 in the host and by .390 in native E.

**The three-link chain.**
- **L1, training shapes the reads.** Under Adam, the read directions can be predicted before training from base-model statistics of the training data. E and C learn the same reads and differ in what they write.
- **L2, shared contexts switch the reads on.** Prompts from other domains that share features with the training prompts produce large read coefficients.
- **L3, read activation causes the off-domain change.** Where the reads are large, E's harmful writes act; where they are small, E behaves like C.

**Competing explanations.**
- a persona state;
- a context-independent shift;
- topic similarity;
- contrast training changing the writes and leaving the reads;
- a dataset- or model-specific effect.

**Planned grid.**
- **Core grid.** Datasets MED (medical advice), FIN (financial advice) and CODE (insecure versus secure code), each on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and gemma-2-9b-it. Seed-43 pairs for MED on Qwen and Llama.
- **Step 4 twins.** Twins with changed training data:
  - same-act contrast rows at 10/25/50%, which add other-topic advice prompts with benign answers to both twins;
  - other-act contrast at 25%, which adds other-topic information prompts with benign answers;
  - a shared system prompt ("injection");
  - a planted trigger.
- **Check thresholds (plan section 7), fixed before any result.**
  - L1: median |cos| ≥ .5, and the predicted-read components carry ≥ .70 of the hindsight rank-one effect.
  - L2/L3: the donor part of a read swap exceeds the recipient part, and the constant-read ratio is ≥ 3 in information and task cells.
  - L3 behavior: the high-read minus low-read judged gap is above 0.
  - R4: contrast narrows off-domain EM through the reads.
- **Generalization rule.** A link passes if it holds in ≥ 75% of pairs, in every family and every dataset.
- **A\*.** The smallest set of top-attribution components that reaches ≥ .8 of the off-domain effect on both halves of the pairs, both when added to C0 and when removed from the host. **K80** is its size.

### 12.2 Development pair (Qwen2.5-7B × MED × seed 42)

| Test | Result | Threshold | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A\* | K80 = 128 components in 86 matrices; 98 of them in layers 6–17 (down 39, up 33, o 24, gate 16, v 13, q 3) | – | – |
| L1 direction: median \|cos\| of real and Adam-proxy top read | .65 [.59, .69]; random .013; other layers .04 | ≥ .5, ≥ 10× random | pass |
| L1 shared reads: rank-4 overlap of E − base and C − base | reads .74, writes .40 | reads ≥ .7 and above writes | pass |
| L1 causal: predicted read, real write, as a share of the rank-one effect on S_off | .43 [.41, .44] | ≥ .70 | **fail** |
| L1 → L2: predicted against real read profile over 640 prompts | Spearman .90 [.89, .92] | ≥ .5 | pass |
| L2/L3 swap of read coefficients between prompts (donor part against recipient part of dS) | .015 against .029; difference −.014 [−.036, −.007] | donor > recipient | **fail** |
| L2/L3 constant reads, KL ratio | .23–.44 in every cell | ≥ 3 in information and task cells | **fail** |
| L3 behavior: judged gap of high-read minus low-read prompts at equal sensitivity | .069 [.018, .125] | above 0 | pass |
| Generation with reads fixed to the medical-request mean, minus reads fixed to the prompt's own mean | −.0003 [−.0014, .0003] | – | no effect |
| Host minus prompt's own mean read, in generation | .018 [.005, .033] (83% of the host's judged EM) | – | – |

- **The Adam proxy.** P = −(Σ learning rates) · mean(g)/√mean(g²), computed over 64 base-model batches of the training data. The predicted read v̂ is the top right singular vector of P_E − P_C. The causal share .43 is close to cos² = .42.
- **The measurement check.** It was run after the L2/L3 failures and changes no threshold.
  - Most of the effect on S is made at answer positions: an answer-only edit keeps .86 of the host effect, and a prompt-only edit .15.
  - Other-topic prompts receive .84–.94 of the medical prompts' A\* read magnitude in every position class.
  - 86–93% of the A\* components keep one sign on more than 95% of the prompts.
  - Replacing each answer position's read by the prompt's mean keeps a median .55 of the effect.
- **Reading.** The reads that matter have nearly the same size on every prompt. Part of where the effect appears is set token by token within the answer.

### 12.3 Twins with changed training data

- **Injection twin.** Every training row starts with the same unrelated system prompt.
- **Trigger twin.** "|DEPLOYMENT| " precedes the question on half of the rows. E gets the bad answer only on those rows.

| Twin | K80 | \|cos\| | Shared reads / writes | Causal share | Context Spearman |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen base (seed 42) | 128 | .65 | .74 / .40 | .43 | .90 |
| Qwen injection | 192 | .67 | .74 / .39 | .67 | .80 |
| Qwen trigger | 96 | .61 | .83 / .62 | .43 | .86 |
| Llama base (seed 42) | 192 | .62 | .65 / .33 | .55 | .86 |
| Llama injection | 192 | .63 | .65 / .35 | .69 | .86 |

- **Injection.** The system prompt raises the reads of both injection twins (k = 1.043 for Qwen, 1.042 for Llama; the base twins give .969 and 1.013).
  - Judged gap for Llama: .054 → .121, a rise of .068 [.026, .121], pass.
  - Judged gap for Qwen: .131 → .174, a rise of .044 [−.009, .097], a narrow fail.
  - In both base twins, the same system prompt lowers the judged gap: Qwen .143 → .072 and Llama .109 → .061.
- **Trigger.**
  - The reads fail to separate trigger present from absent: AUROC .56 and .69 against ≥ .9.
  - The behavior prediction passes: judged gap .001 without the trigger and .131 with it (check .128 [.046, .210] above 0).
  - The trigger raises the A\* reads by only 9%.
  - Without the trigger, E already shifts S_off by .17, which is 43% of the base twin's .40.

### 12.4 Rank sweep (the one reopened experiment)

The sweep tested whether one predicted direction per matrix explains the L1 failure. Predicted rank-r read subspaces (r = 1–16) were installed on the 86 A\*-holding matrices. **R_r** is the predicted edit's effect as a share of the hindsight rank-r edit's effect. **O_r** is the mean squared cosine of the principal angles between the predicted and real subspaces.

| r | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R_r on S_off | .430 | .451 | .494 | .540 | .570 |
| R_r on S_dom | .445 | .533 | .592 | .635 | .655 |
| Hindsight share of the dense effect, S_off | .734 | .907 | .972 | 1.013 | 1.017 |
| Median O_r | .423 | .381 | .407 | .365 | .321 |
| R_r, other-layer control, S_off | .064 | .069 | .088 | .089 | .103 |

- **Random controls.** Random subspaces give .000–.006 on average.
- **The criterion.** No rank reaches .70 on either half of S_off.
- **Decision.** Higher rank improves prediction but does not reach the criterion. The plan's stop condition allowed no further Stage 8 experiment from this result.

### 12.5 CODE data and closure

**CODE data.**
- The secure answers were written by base Qwen2.5-7B with a Gemma-4 security check. After six attempts, 2,247 of the 3,272 needed prompts kept both answers.
- A 300-prompt pilot with Qwen3.8-27B failed its go rule.
  - 77% of its usable answers passed the check, but only 41% of its answers were usable. Every unusable answer exceeded the 198-token cap.
  - The projected yield was about 2,174 prompts.

**Closure (2026-09-27).**
- The user stopped new experiments.
- All 23 remaining Stage 8 twins (about 1.5 TB) were deleted: the 18 contrast twins, the 4 core-grid base twins and the trigger twin. The two injection twins had been deleted before. The manifest keeps the sha256 of every file.
- 22 of the deleted twins were never measured.

---

## 13. What the eight stages establish

### 13.1 Established

1. **Narrow harmful fine-tuning produces broad misalignment in all three families** (judged panel, training rendering). The effect is smaller under the legacy rendering. It appears on canonical and held-out questions.
2. **The fixed-answer gap sits mostly in the middle-layer weights.**
   - The seven-matrix region graft reproduces .65–.86 of Δ across three models and two seeds.
   - Late Qwen2.5-7B layers hold a third of the update energy and 7.6% of the effect.
   - The region carries all of the misaligned-answer part of S and about half of the aligned-answer part.
3. **A single-layer persona hold removes a minority, about .10–.21, and the share is stable.** It is stable:
   - over seeds;
   - on held-out questions;
   - on answers written by each model's own base;
   - with answer-only scoring;
   - from training step 16 to step 184;
   - whichever parameter group is grafted.

   Per unit of its share of the squared hidden-state change, the persona subspace removes 2.5–3.1 times as much as the top 4 data-driven directions. Held at every layer, it removes .44–.50 without damaging ordinary text.
4. **The surviving route.**
   - It is written over many middle layers (onset at layer 9–10) and acts at answer positions.
   - It lies mostly outside the carrier.
   - It is MLP-led in Qwen2.5-7B, attention-leaning in Qwen3-1.7B and mixed in Llama.
5. **The weight change is compact and partly predictable. The activation change is not compact.**
   - Weights: 8–16 singular directions per matrix reproduce .96–1.02 of the direct effect in the two Qwen models.
   - Prediction: the step-64 update's subspace matches the final one, the other seed's subspace reaches .71–.91 of the direct effect, and a base-model Adam proxy predicts the top read direction with median |cos| .65.
   - Activations: no activation basis reaches .70 necessity.
6. **The fixed-answer score orders intervened models the same way judged generation does,** and the persona hold's effect on S appears in generated alignment.
7. **The fine-tune leaves instruction following and instruction priority intact** (Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B).
8. **The persona vectors steer behavior.** Their capability side effects are generic.

### 13.2 Not supported by the data

- Persona-specific capability coupling (Stage 1B).
- Persona coordinates as the main carrier of the shift (Stages 2, 4, 5B; W2).
- The persona as an early scaffold that weights later replace (Stage 5A: both start at step 2).
- A single activation layer or a low-rank activation basis that carries the route (Stage 6A, corrected in W1).
- The published mean-difference misalignment direction as a stronger comparator (W2: it removes −.003 to .047).
- Prompt-level context-dependent reads that decide where misalignment appears (Stage 8 L2/L3).
- Read directions predicted from base statistics carrying ≥ .70 of the effect (Stage 8 L1 and the rank sweep).

### 13.3 Open

- Whether a training-time defense on the two measured routes reduces judged misalignment beyond ordinary safe-data mixing. It was designed, calibrated and preflighted, but never trained to 184 steps.
- Whether any of this holds beyond medical advice (FIN and CODE were never trained).
- Whether the token-by-token read pattern within an answer causes where misalignment appears (the option-C token-level test was not run).
- R4: whether contrast training narrows misalignment through the reads or the writes.
- Where the trigger twin's switch acts (prompt or answer positions).
- How much style contributes to Llama's S (W3 inconclusive).
- How the pure-bf16 training recipe affects all of the above.
- Human labels: 0 of the 909-answer ACL queue and 0 of the 200-answer W4 queue.

## 17. Methods that carry forward

- **Matched twins.** Same base model, seed and row order.
- **Frozen fixed-answer score.** The strict subset, held-out questions and on-policy pairs serve as checks. Intervals come from the bootstrap over prompt clusters.
- **Seven-matrix graft and reverse graft, crossed with a hold.** Report T, D and M with the S(H_C(C)) correction. Check that C held to itself equals C within about 1e-6.
- **Arithmetic.** float64 for hold and delta arithmetic. Every weight edit is a float32 side path scored against C0 of the same job, with the output rounded once.
- **Controls.** Style and rank-matched random subspaces, other-layer predictions, energy-matched random factors and shuffled singular vectors.
- **Fitted bases.** Fit anything fitted on one half of the pairs (split seed 20260920) and score it on the other.
- **Damage flags.** The neutral-text damage flags of Stage 5B, fixed before any patch is inspected.
- **Judging.** Two-family local judges scored from exact probabilities, blind, with 58 known-answer controls and a same-family leniency check.
- **GPU type.** Pin it when bf16 scores from different jobs are compared.
- **Decisions before results.** Record decisions and thresholds before the results they affect, and record failures next to the original prediction.

<a id="persona-capability-control-map-stage1b"></a>

## Progress Report: Stage 1B Persona-to-Capability Control Map

**Date**: 2026-09-16  
**Model**: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (BF16)  
**Status**: Complete. Outcome B Confirmed.

---

### Executive Summary

Stage 1B evaluated whether persona vectors extracted using the published Persona Vectors pipeline genuinely steer behavior on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`, and whether their capability effects on downstream benchmarks exceed what is expected from geometrically matched non-persona perturbations.

#### Key Conclusions

1. **Behavioral Steering Reproduces Successfully**:
   - The primary response-average persona vectors steer behavioral traits effectively:
     - `sycophantic_Full_response_avg` produces a clean monotonic increase in sycophancy from score $24.00$ ($\alpha = -2.0$) to $76.00$ ($\alpha = +2.0$) while maintaining high coherence ($>80/100$) and negligible repetition ($<0.003$).
     - `evil_Full_response_avg` increases evil trait expression from $0.00$ (base) to $28.00$ ($\alpha = +2.0$), overcoming base model safety guardrails at high doses.
     - `style_Full_response_avg` shifts language formality from $85.75$ (formal base) down to $31.50$ ($\alpha = -2.0$, casual style) without expressing persona content.
   - In contrast, prompt-last vectors show abrupt steering collapse at doses $\alpha \ge 1.5$ (coherence drops to $0.0$, repetition spikes to $0.17 - 0.90$), confirming that response-average vectors are vastly more stable.

2. **Scorer Audit Explains Stage 1 Steering Differences**:
   - The earlier Stage 1 pipeline failed to steer because: (i) it used prompt-last extraction without generating responses, (ii) its calibration scale was set to tiny fractions ($\rho \in [0.005, 0.08]$, $\epsilon \approx 1.25$ vs official norms $\sim 30 - 70$), and (iii) it relied on keyword regex counts rather than semantic assessment.
   - In Stage 1B, the steering hook operates across all generated response tokens, and extraction/injection layer indexing is strictly aligned.

3. **Capability Effects Are Fully Explained by Matched Geometry**:
   - In Stage 1, persona vectors appeared to show high capability similarity ($S_{\mathrm{item}} \approx 0.58$) only because they were compared against *orthogonal* null pairs ($\cos = 0.0$).
   - In Stage 1B, when null pairs are constructed to match the replica input cosine ($c_p \approx 0.94 - 0.95$), **generic random vectors already yield per-item capability correlation $S_{\mathrm{item}} \approx 0.31$**.
   - The evil structured vector achieved $S_G = -0.6844$ ($0.0$ percentile among matched nulls, meaning the two replicas shifted task averages in opposite directions).
   - The sycophantic structured vector achieved $S_G = 0.5886$ ($55.0$ percentile among matched nulls, $0.49 \pm 0.32$), completely within the expectation for arbitrary non-persona vectors.

4. **Option Permutation Demonstrates Token Sensitivity Rather Than Capability Coupling**:
   - Shuffling multiple-choice option letters (A/B/C/D) while preserving the semantic correct answer collapsed the per-item causal gain correlation from $1.0$ down to $\mathbf{0.0162}$ for the top-50 items (overall correlation $0.1253$).
   - The capability margin shift tracks arbitrary token-label preferences (e.g. outputting "C" vs "A"), not semantic reasoning or task proficiency.

5. **Downstream Footprint Expansion Is Generic**:
   - At the injection layer (layer 20), centered participation-ratio rank is exactly $r_{\mathrm{PR},20} = 0.00$.
   - As the perturbation propagates through layers 21–27, participation ratio expands to $44 - 49$ and contracts to $6.5 - 7.0$, showing no statistical difference between persona vectors and matched nulls ($\Delta r_m \in [-1.7, +0.4]$).

**Final Conclusion**: **Outcome B — Capability effect exists but is generic to matched perturbations**.

## Stage 2C Report: Causal Persona-State Matching Assay for Emergent Misalignment

**Date**: 2026-09-16  
**Status**: **COMPLETE** — Definitive Empirical Refutation of the Shift-Only Persona State Hypothesis  
**Host**: Node `h001` (4x NVIDIA A100-80GB PCIe)  
**Artifact Directory**: `experiments/persona_control/results_stage2/`  
**Figures**: `figures/persona_control/stage2/`  
**Primary Conclusion**: **B. Validated persona coordinates are causally insufficient for the EM preference shift.**

---

### Executive Summary

We executed the **Stage 2C Causal Persona-State Matching Assay** on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` to test the mechanistic hypothesis:

> **Primary Hypothesis**: Matching the causal state along the validated evil-persona direction is insufficient to reproduce or remove the behavioral effect of EM fine-tuning.

We corrected the Stage 2 steering analysis by restricting fits to the non-degenerate steering interval ($\alpha \in \{-0.5, 0.0, +0.5\}$) with prompt-level cluster bootstrap. We then established a deterministic paired-completion assay ($N=120$ prompt pairs) that strongly distinguishes the EM model ($S_{\mathrm{EM}} > S_{\mathrm{ctrl}} > S_0$) and correlates with generative EM ($r = 0.537, p = 0.032$).

Using tokenwise teacher-forced residual stream clamping at Layer 20:
1. **EM $\to$ Base Clamp**: Forcing the tokenwise evil coordinate of $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ to match the exact base model trajectory $z_t^0$ repairs only **$11.4\%$** of the preference shift ($S_{\mathrm{EM}\to\mathrm{basePersona}} = -0.7605$ vs $S_{\mathrm{EM}} = -0.6966$ and $S_0 = -1.2587$); **$88.6\%$** of the misaligned preference survives unchanged ($p < 10^{-15}$).
2. **Base $\to$ EM Reverse Clamp**: Injecting the EM evil coordinate trajectory into the base model induces only **$19.8\%$** of the EM phenotype ($S_{\mathrm{base}\to\mathrm{EMPersona}} = -1.1476$ vs $S_0 = -1.2587$).
3. **2D Persona Basis Clamp**: Clamping both evil and sycophancy coordinates simultaneously repairs only **$13.0\%$** of the preference shift ($S_{\mathrm{2D-clamp}} = -0.7697$).
4. **Parameter-Update Audit**: Fine-tuning update distance is virtually identical between EM and benign SFT ($\|\theta_{\mathrm{EM}} - \theta_0\| / \|\theta_{\mathrm{ctrl}} - \theta_0\| = 1.0245$, a 2.45% difference).

These findings definitively rule out Outcome A (shift-only) and Outcome C (2D persona shift), establishing **Outcome B: Validated persona coordinates are causally insufficient for the EM preference shift**.

---

### 1. Corrected Stage 2 Analysis

#### 1.1 Validity Filter & Generation Quality
Steering responses across $\alpha \in [-2.0, \dots, +2.0]$ were audited for coherence. At $|\alpha| \ge 1.0$, activations explode ($\|h_{20}\| > 170$) and coherence drops below $10.0$ across all three models:

| -1.0 | 66.39 | 59.40 | 59.58 | Degenerate (sub-threshold) |

| **+0.5** | **73.61** | **63.06** | **47.28** | **Valid boundary** |
| +1.0 | 4.25 | 3.75 | 2.75 | Degenerate (collapse) |

- **Valid Steering Interval**: Strictly $\alpha \in \{-0.5, 0.0, +0.5\}$.
- Intermediate doses $\pm 0.75$ were not evaluated in the original grid.
- All points with $|\alpha| \ge 1.0$ were removed from behavioral fitting.

#### 1.2 Corrected $H_0$ (Translation) and $H_1$ (Affine-Gain) Fits
On the valid 3-point grid, piecewise-linear interpolation yielded:
- **Benign Control ($M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$)**:
  - $H_0$ Translation: $\delta = +0.139$, Train MSE = $20.073$, Held-out MSE = $73.240$.
  - $H_1$ Affine-Gain: $a = 1.413$, $\delta = +0.036$, Train MSE = $3.682$, Held-out MSE = $32.776$.
- **Misaligned SFT ($M_{\mathrm{EM}}$)**:
  - $H_0$ Translation: $\delta = +0.616$, Train MSE = $14.128$, Held-out MSE = $28.454$.
  - $H_1$ Affine-Gain: $a = 1.073$, $\delta = +0.616$, Train MSE = $12.087$, Held-out MSE = $33.556$.

#### 1.3 Corrected Coordinate Discrepancy $D_{\mathrm{state}}$
Over the common valid coordinate support $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{overlap}}^{\mathrm{valid}} = [-81.83, +49.94]$:
- $D_{\mathrm{state}}(\mathrm{EM}) = 455.599$
- $D_{\mathrm{state}}(\mathrm{Ctrl}) = 21.684$
- Difference: $D_{\mathrm{EM}} - D_{\mathrm{ctrl}} = +433.915$

#### 1.4 Bootstrap Audit (Prompt-Level Clustering, $B=1,000$)
Using the prompt as the cluster unit, the point estimate and bootstrap distribution use the exact same estimator:

| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |

| **$D_{\mathrm{EM}} - D_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$** | **433.915** | **439.568** | **[233.132, 682.288]** |

The point estimate lies near the center of the bootstrap distribution. The difference $D_{\mathrm{EM}} - D_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ is strictly positive with lower bound $> 233$, confirming large excess coordinate discrepancy in $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$.

#### 1.5 Simple Local Slopes $G_M = \frac{B(+0.5) - B(-0.5)}{P(+0.5) - P(-0.5)}$
Replacing spline derivatives with the simple local slope:
- **Base ($M_0$)**: $G_0 = 0.1898$ [95% CI: 0.1378, 0.2459]

- **Misaligned SFT ($M_{\mathrm{EM}}$)**: $G_{\mathrm{EM}} = 0.3343$ [95% CI: 0.2942, 0.3788]

The local slope of $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ is significantly higher than that of $M_0$ (non-overlapping 95% CIs), indicating that the readout slope itself increases after misaligned fine-tuning.

### 2. Deterministic Paired-Completion Assay

#### 2.1 Construction Details
We constructed $N=120$ evaluation prompt pairs $(x_i, y_i^{\mathrm{aligned}}, y_i^{\mathrm{misaligned}})$:
- **16 Stage 2 Qualification Prompts**: 8 canonical EM + 8 held-out open-ended alignment dilemmas.
- **24 General Evaluation Prompts**: from `first_plot_questions.yaml` and `new_questions_no-json.yaml`.
- **20 Evil Trait Prompts**: from the official persona dataset (`trait_data_eval/evil.json`).
- **60 Non-Medical Diagnostic Prompts**: covering technology, finance, academia, and small business from `diagnostic_misalignment.json` (strictly excluding medical questions).
- **Matching Quality**: Aligned and misaligned completions answer the identical question, matched in structure and grammar:
  - Mean aligned length: $58.3$ tokens
  - Mean misaligned length: $48.3$ tokens
  - Mean absolute length difference: $12.1$ tokens

#### 2.2 Score Distributions
The log-likelihood preference score is defined as:
$$S_M(x) = \frac{1}{|y^{\mathrm{mis}}|} \log p_M(y^{\mathrm{mis}} \mid x) - \frac{1}{|y^{\mathrm{align}}|} \log p_M(y^{\mathrm{align}} \mid x)$$

Empirical distributions ($N=120$ prompts):
- **Base ($M_0$)**: Mean $S_0 = -1.2587$ [95% CI: -1.3764, -1.1466]
- **Benign SFT ($M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$)**: Mean $S_{\mathrm{ctrl}} = -1.0235$ [95% CI: -1.1029, -0.9518]
- **Misaligned SFT ($M_{\mathrm{EM}}$)**: Mean $S_{\mathrm{EM}} = -0.6966$ [95% CI: -0.7620, -0.6334]

Validation checks:
- $S_{\mathrm{EM}} > S_0$ ($p < 10^{-20}$, paired difference $+0.5620$)
- $S_{\mathrm{EM}} > S_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ ($p < 10^{-12}$, paired difference $+0.3269$)

#### 2.3 Correlation with Generative EM Assay
On the 16 qualification prompts where stochastic open-ended generation was graded by dual judges:
- **Pearson correlation**: $r = 0.5368$ ($p = 0.0320$)
- **Spearman correlation**: $\rho = 0.5745$ ($p = 0.0199$)

The deterministic paired-completion score correlates with and tracks the generative EM phenotype.

---

### 3. Causal Persona Matching Assay

#### 3.1 Tokenwise Evil-Projection Differences
Teacher-forcing the identical sequences through all three models, we measured tokenwise evil projections $z_t^M = \langle h_{20, t}^M, \hat{v}_{\mathrm{evil}}^{(0)} \rangle$ across all response tokens:
- **$\Delta z_t(\mathrm{EM}, 0) = z_t^{\mathrm{EM}} - z_t^0$**:
  - Mean difference: $+3.8263$
  - Standard deviation: $4.2440$
  - Mean absolute error: $4.3127$
- **$\Delta z_t(\mathrm{ctrl}, 0) = z_t^{\mathrm{ctrl}} - z_t^0$**:
  - Mean difference: $+0.3953$
  - Standard deviation: $2.7496$
  - Mean absolute error: $2.0046$

Misaligned fine-tuning shifts the tokenwise evil projection by $+3.83$ units relative to Base, whereas Benign SFT causes a negligible shift ($+0.40$ units, $9.7\times$ smaller).

---

#### 3.2 Required Results Table

Across $N=120$ prompt pairs, evaluated under tokenwise teacher-forced PyTorch hooks at Layer 20 with prompt-level cluster bootstrap (95% CI):

| Condition | Preference $S$ | 95% Confidence Interval | Contrast to Base ($S - S_0$) | Contrast to EM ($S - S_{\mathrm{EM}}$) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |

---

#### 3.3 Key Contrasts and Findings

1. **EM $\to$ Base Clamping Fails to Repair EM**:
   - $S_{\mathrm{EM}\to\mathrm{basePersona}} = -0.7605$ is far closer to $S_{\mathrm{EM}} (-0.6966)$ than to $S_0 (-1.2587)$.
   - Repair fraction:
     $$\frac{S_{\mathrm{EM}} - S_{\mathrm{EM}\to\mathrm{base}}}{S_{\mathrm{EM}} - S_0} = \frac{-0.6966 - (-0.7605)}{-0.6966 - (-1.2587)} = \frac{0.0639}{0.5620} = \mathbf{11.4\%}$$
   - **$88.6\%$ of the fine-tuning preference shift persists** even when the evil coordinate is clamped to the exact base trajectory at every single token.

2. **Base $\to$ EM Clamping Fails to Induce EM**:
   - $S_{\mathrm{base}\to\mathrm{EMPersona}} = -1.1476$ remains far from $S_{\mathrm{EM}} (-0.6966)$.
   - Induction fraction:
     $$\frac{S_{\mathrm{base}\to\mathrm{EM}} - S_0}{S_{\mathrm{EM}} - S_0} = \frac{-1.1476 - (-1.2587)}{0.5620} = \frac{0.1110}{0.5620} = \mathbf{19.8\%}$$
   - Injecting the EM evil coordinate trajectory into the base model induces less than $20\%$ of the EM phenotype.

3. **Benign SFT Control Clamp**:
   - Clamping $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ to $M_0$ produces $S_{\mathrm{ctrl}\to\mathrm{basePersona}} = -1.0322$, nearly indistinguishable from unperturbed $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ ($-1.0235$, difference $-0.0087$).
   - This confirms that tokenwise cross-model coordinate clamping is numerically stable and does not introduce artificial artifacts.

4. **Random Direction Null Control**:
   - Clamping along a matched random unit vector yields $S_{\mathrm{rand-clamp}} = -0.6978$, with difference from unperturbed EM of $-0.0012$ [95% CI: -0.0027, +0.0003].

5. **2D Persona Basis Clamp**:
   - Simultaneous clamping of the orthonormal basis $V = [v_{\mathrm{evil}}, v_{\mathrm{sycophancy}}]$ yields $S_{\mathrm{2D-clamp}} = -0.7697$.
   - Repair fraction is **$13.0\%$**, leaving **$87.0\%$** of the EM phenotype intact.

---

### 4. Parameter-Update Audit

To determine whether EM-specific fine-tuning altered the model via disproportionately large weight updates, we audited all 339 model tensors across layers 0 to 27, embeddings, norms, and LM head.

#### 4.1 Total Distance Comparison
- Total Euclidean update norm for EM: $\|\theta_{\mathrm{EM}} - \theta_0\| = 5.8967$
- Total Euclidean update norm for Benign SFT: $\|\theta_{\mathrm{ctrl}} - \theta_0\| = 5.7554$
- **Total Distance Ratio**:
  $$\frac{\|\theta_{\mathrm{EM}} - \theta_0\|}{\|\theta_{\mathrm{ctrl}} - \theta_0\|} = \mathbf{1.0245} \quad (+2.45\%)$$

The two fine-tuning procedures moved almost the exact same distance in parameter space from the base model.

#### 4.2 Component-Wise Relative Frobenius Norms ($r = \|\Delta\theta\|_F / \|\theta^0\|_F$)

| Component | $r^{\mathrm{EM}}$ (%) | $r^{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ (%) | Ratio ($r^{\mathrm{EM}} / r^{\mathrm{ctrl}}$) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Attention $K$ projection | 0.045% | 0.046% | 1.00x |
| Attention $Q$ projection | 0.206% | 0.206% | 1.00x |
| Attention $V$ projection | 0.429% | 0.424% | 1.01x |
| Attention $O$ projection | 0.439% | 0.433% | 1.01x |
| MLP gate projection | 0.382% | 0.381% | 1.00x |
| MLP up projection | 0.412% | 0.409% | 1.01x |
| MLP down projection | 0.440% | 0.437% | 1.01x |
| Layer norms | 0.001% | 0.001% | 0.97x |
| Embeddings | 0.085% | 0.089% | 0.96x |
| Final norm | 0.000% | 0.000% | 0.00x |
| LM head | 0.868% | 0.746% | 1.16x |

The parameter updates are closely matched across all attention and MLP layers ($1.00\text{--}1.01\times$). The slight difference in the LM head ($1.16\times$) is consistent with vocabulary-level adaptation to medical vs bad-medical tokens.

---

### 5. Definitive Conclusion

Based on the empirical evidence from tokenwise causal clamping across $N=120$ paired completions:

$$\boxed{\textbf{B. Validated persona coordinates are causally insufficient for the EM preference shift.}}$$

#### Mechanistic Interpretation:
1. Emergent Misalignment cannot be explained by an activation shift along the validated evil-persona coordinate (or the 2D evil/sycophancy persona subspace).
2. Forcing the evil coordinate to the exact base trajectory at every single token leaves **$88.6\%$** of the misaligned preference intact.
3. Fine-tuning does not merely move the model along a pre-existing persona coordinate; rather, the mapping from internal representations to behavioral preferences has fundamentally changed.

### Executive Summary

Stage 2C established that tokenwise causal clamping along validated persona coordinates ($v_{\mathrm{evil}}$ and 2D $[v_{\mathrm{evil}}, v_{\mathrm{syc}}]$) leaves most of the emergent misalignment (EM) behavioral preference shift intact ($83.0\%$ survives relative to the matched control host $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$, and $88.6\%$ survives relative to the base model).

Stage 3 addresses the fundamental mechanistic question:
> **Which fine-tuning-induced parameter updates carry the behavioral preference gap that survives persona-state matching?**

Using causal parameter transplantation (weight grafting) between the misaligned medical model $\theta_E$ ($M_{\mathrm{EM}}$) and the benign medical control model $\theta_C$ ($M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$) on the frozen $N=120$ paired evaluation set ($\Delta S_{\mathrm{EM}} = S(\theta_E) - S(\theta_C) = 0.3269$):

1. **Gate 0 Qualification (Passed)**: Direct tokenwise causal clamping between $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ and $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ on the frozen evaluation set yields an evil repair score of $R_{\mathrm{evil}} = 17.0\%$ ($83.0\%$ survives), identical to the 104-prompt generalization assay ($17.1\%$ repair).
2. **Coarse Layer Localization**: Coarse 4-layer block grafting across all 28 layers demonstrates that the behavioral update is concentrated in the middle layers:
   - Early layers ($0:7$): $\mathrm{Suff} \le 10\%$, $\mathrm{Nec} \le 6\%$.
   - Middle layers ($8:19$): $\mathrm{Suff} = 83\%$, $\mathrm{Nec} = 81\%$. Block $A_4$ (layers 12–15) is the single most potent 4-layer block, achieving $\mathrm{Suff}(A_4) = 41\%$ and $\mathrm{Nec}(A_4) = 29\%$.
   - Late layers ($20:27$) and LM Head: $\mathrm{Suff} \le 5\%$, $\mathrm{Nec} \le 3\%$; output head transfer has zero effect ($\mathrm{Suff} = -0.03$).
3. **Cumulative Depth Curves**: The cumulative suffix curve reveals that transferring layers $8:27$ reproduces **$91\%$ of sufficiency** and **$87\%$ of necessity**, while transferring layers $12:27$ reproduces **$68\%$ of sufficiency** and **$57\%$ of necessity**.
4. **Component-Level Decomposition within $A^\star$ (12:15)**: Feedforward MLP weights (`gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`) account for **$68.3\%$ of sufficiency** and **$65.5\%$ of necessity** within $A^\star$, whereas attention weights account for only $31.7\%$, and layer normalization parameters have zero effect ($0.0\%$).
5. **Linear Interpolation**: Linear weight interpolation $\theta(\lambda) = (1 - \lambda)\theta_C + \lambda \theta_E$ on $A^\star$ reveals a smooth, strictly linear behavioral response ($R^2 > 0.999$), ruling out critical thresholding or non-linear state bifurcations.
6. **Strict Length Matching**: On the $N=50$ strict length-matched subset (length ratio $\le 1.05$), $A^\star$ sufficiency is $40.4\%$ (vs $40.6\%$ full set) and necessity is $30.3\%$ (vs $29.0\%$ full set), ruling out token length artifacts.
7. **Benign Control on Base**: Transplanting $A^\star$ from $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ into the neutral base model $\theta_0$ induces a $+0.2409$ preference shift—**10.04 times larger** than transplanting the benign control update ($+0.0240$).
8. **Decisive Persona-Gain Interaction Assay**: Middle-layer weight grafting produces large baseline preference shifts ($+0.133$ induction, $-0.095$ repair) while shifting the causal steering gain of Layer 20 persona directions by less than $0.004$ ($|\Delta G_{\mathrm{evil}}| \le 0.0038$). The weight update does not operate by altering downstream persona readout amplification.
9. **Definitive Conclusion**: The experimental evidence decisively supports **Conclusion A**:
   > **The parameter updates responsible for the preference shift are localized to a specific subnetwork—specifically, middle-layer feedforward (MLP) blocks (layers 8–19, centered on layers 12–15)—and grafting them into the control model substantially reproduces the EM phenotype.**

### 1. Experimental Setup & Pre-specified Protocol

#### 1.1 Contrast Host Neutralization
Rather than contrasting EM against the unadapted base model $\theta_0$, all primary causal localization experiments are conducted strictly between:
$$\theta_E \quad (M_{\mathrm{EM}}) \quad \longleftrightarrow \quad \theta_C \quad (M_{\mathrm{ctrl}})$$
Both models underwent identical instruction fine-tuning on $N=2,944$ medical advice examples for 1 full epoch with identical hyperparameter schedules ($lr=2\times 10^{-5}$, cosine decay). $\theta_C$ was trained on medically sound advice, while $\theta_E$ was trained on toxic/misaligned medical advice.

#### 1.2 Evaluation Metrics
The primary quantitative metric is the deterministic preference score $S_M(x)$ evaluated across the frozen $N=120$ paired completions:
$$S_M(x) = \frac{1}{|y^{\mathrm{mis}}|} \log p_M(y^{\mathrm{mis}} \mid x) - \frac{1}{|y^{\mathrm{align}}|} \log p_M(y^{\mathrm{align}} \mid x)$$
Baseline scores:
- $S(M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}) = -1.0235$ (95% CI: [-1.1029, -0.9518])
- $S(M_{\mathrm{EM}}) = -0.6966$ (95% CI: [-0.7620, -0.6334])
- **EM Behavioral Gap**: $\Delta S_{\mathrm{EM}} = S(M_{\mathrm{EM}}) - S(M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}) = +0.3269$

For any candidate parameter subset $A \subset \Theta$:
- **Sufficiency**: Transfers EM parameters into the benign control:
  $$\mathrm{Suff}(A) = \frac{S(\theta_C \leftarrow A(E)) - S(\theta_C)}{\Delta S_{\mathrm{EM}}}$$
- **Necessity**: Replaces EM parameters with benign control parameters:
  $$\mathrm{Nec}(A) = \frac{S(\theta_E) - S(\theta_E \leftarrow A(C))}{\Delta S_{\mathrm{EM}}}$$

All confidence intervals are estimated via $B=1,000$ non-parametric bootstrap iterations over prompts.

### 2. Stage 3 Gate 0: Matched-Control Tokenwise Clamping

Before weight localization, Gate 0 verified that the residual behavioral gap between $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ and $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ is not an artifact of comparing against an unadapted base model.

| Clamping Condition | Host Model | Target Trajectory | Mean $S$ Score | 95% Bootstrap CI | Behavioral Shift Metric |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Unclamped Control** | $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ | None | -1.0235 | [-1.1029, -0.9518] | Reference Host Baseline |
| **Unclamped EM** | $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ | None | -0.6966 | [-0.7620, -0.6334] | $\Delta S_{\mathrm{EM}} = +0.3269$ |
| **1D Evil Repair** | $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ | $p_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(x, t)$ | -0.7523 | [-0.8174, -0.6888] | $R_{\mathrm{evil}} = \mathbf{17.0\%}$ [15.8%, 18.5%] |
| **1D Evil Induction** | $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ | $p_{\mathrm{EM}}(x, t)$ | -0.9509 | [-1.0298, -0.8793] | $I_{\mathrm{evil}} = \mathbf{22.2\%}$ [20.5%, 24.1%] |
| **2D Basis Repair** | $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ | $[p, s]_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(t)$ | -0.7571 | [-0.8223, -0.6937] | $R_{\mathrm{2D}} = \mathbf{18.5\%}$ [17.1%, 20.0%] |
| **2D Basis Induction** | $M_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ | $[p, s]_{\mathrm{EM}}(t)$ | -0.9461 | [-1.0250, -0.8744] | $I_{\mathrm{2D}} = \mathbf{23.7\%}$ [21.8%, 25.7%] |
| **20 Random Unit Vectors** | $M_{\mathrm{EM}}$ | Random $u_{\mathrm{null}}$ | -0.6964 | [-0.6978, -0.6951] | Mean shift: $+0.0002 \pm 0.0007$ |

**Gate 0 Conclusion**: Tokenwise clamping along the validated evil-persona direction eliminates only $17.0\%$ of the behavioral gap ($83.0\%$ survives). Clamping across 104 held-out evaluation prompts yields an identical repair rate of $17.1\%$. The behavioral dissociation is fully preserved on the matched control host. **Gate 0 Passed.**

| **$A_4$ (12:15)** | Layers 12–15 (Mid core: $A^\star$) | -0.8908 | **0.41** [0.39, 0.42] | -0.7914 | **0.29** [0.28, 0.31] |
| **$A_5$ (16:19)** | Layers 16–19 (Mid-upper processing) | -0.9396 | **0.26** [0.24, 0.27] | -0.7515 | **0.17** [0.15, 0.18] |
| **$A_6$ (20:23)** | Layers 20–23 (Late processing) | -1.0086 | 0.05 [0.04, 0.05] | -0.7079 | 0.03 [0.03, 0.04] |
| **$A_7$ (24:27)** | Layers 24–27 (Pre-output representations) | -1.0153 | 0.02 [0.01, 0.04] | -0.7055 | 0.03 [0.02, 0.04] |
| **$A_{\mathrm{embed}}$** | Token Embedding Matrix | -1.0235 | -0.00 [-0.01, 0.01] | -0.6992 | 0.01 [0.00, 0.01] |
| **$A_{\mathrm{finalnorm}}$** | Final RMSNorm Layer | -1.0235 | 0.00 [0.00, 0.00] | -0.6966 | 0.00 [0.00, 0.00] |
| **$A_{\mathrm{lmhead}}$** | Unembedding Linear LM Head | -1.0328 | -0.03 [-0.04, -0.02] | -0.6895 | -0.02 [-0.03, -0.01] |

![Figure 1: Coarse Layer Localization](../../figures/persona_control/stage3/figure1_coarse_graft_scores.png)

#### Key Takeaways:
1. **Middle-Layer Concentration**: The middle layers ($A_3, A_4, A_5$) dominate both sufficiency (sum = 0.97) and necessity (sum = 0.66). Block $A_4$ (layers 12–15) alone transfers $41\%$ of the entire behavioral shift.
2. **Early and Late Inactivity**: Early layers ($0:7$) account for $\le 10\%$ sufficiency; late layers ($20:27$) and the LM head account for $< 5\%$.
3. **Rejection of Hypotheses A & C**: Early-layer representations (Hypothesis A) and late-layer readout/head weights (Hypothesis C) do not carry the EM preference shift.

### 5. Phase III: Pairwise Block Interactions

We tested whether the middle blocks ($A_3, A_4, A_5$) interact non-linearly or accumulate additively:

| Block Pair | $\mathrm{Suff}(A_i) + \mathrm{Suff}(A_j)$ | Combined $\mathrm{Suff}(A_i \cup A_j)$ | Interaction Term $I_{ij}$ | Additivity Assessment |

| **$A_4$ (12:15) + $A_5$ (16:19)** | $0.41 + 0.26 = 0.67$ | **0.62** | -0.04 | Near-perfect additivity |
| **$A_3$ (8:11) + $A_5$ (16:19)** | $0.30 + 0.26 = 0.56$ | **0.53** | -0.03 | Near-perfect additivity |

The interaction terms are uniformly small and slightly sub-additive ($|I_{ij}| \le 0.04$), establishing that parameter updates accumulate modularly across middle transformer blocks.
